Good question, as a chemistry professor I can tell you that nitrogen is a chemical element with the symbol N and atomic number 7. It is a colorless, odorless, tasteless, and nonflammable gas at room temperature and pressure. Nitrogen is the lightest and most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere, making up about 78% of the air we breathe. Nitrogen is a highly reactive element, but its reactivity is greatly reduced when it is in its elemental form, which is why it does not readily react with other elements in the atmosphere. However, when nitrogen is in its compound form, such as ammonia (NH3) or nitric acid (HNO3), it can be highly reactive and plays a crucial role in many biological and chemical processes.
